instruction:
Fix `plugins/catalog/src/components/CatalogEntityPage/useEntityFromUrl.ts` for these problems, changing only what they need, following the conventions in the shared brief:
1. major (line 55): The redirect guard `handledFormerRef` (a useRef holding the former ref string) is never reset. After one redirect from old-name to new-name, the page component stays mounted because only the route params change. If the user then follows any in-app link to the old URL again, the lookup returns renamedTo, the guard sees the same formerKey and skips navigate. The hook keeps returning `loading: loading || Boolean(renamedTo)`, which stays true, so the page shows a spinner forever. The guard is also unnecessary: the existing `stringifyEntityRef(renamedTo) === current ref` check already handles the stale value that react-use keeps while the next lookup loads. This is a confident finding based on how the hook works; no test covers this path. — fix: Guard on the identity of the async result instead of the ref string, for example `if (handled.current === value) return; handled.current = value;` with `useRef<typeof value>()`. Alternatively, drop the useRef and rely on the self-ref check. Add a test that navigates to the old URL a second time in the same render and expects a second redirect.
2. major (line 49): `catalogApi.getEntityByFormerRef(formerRef).catch(() => undefined)` assumes the method returns a promise. In this same run, `catalogApiMock.mock()` (plugins/catalog-react/src/testUtils/catalogApiMock.ts) now provides `getEntityByFormerRef: jest.fn()`, which returns `undefined`. In any test that uses `catalogApiMock.mock()` with `getEntityByRef` resolving undefined (the usual 'entity not found' setup in adopter and plugin tests), `.catch` throws a TypeError. useAsyncRetry then reports an error and the page shows an error instead of 'Entity not found'. This changes behaviour for existing consumers of a published test util. — fix: Use `try { renamedTo = await catalogApi.getEntityByFormerRef(formerRef); } catch { renamedTo = undefined; }` so a non-promise return value is tolerated, as useExternalRedirect.ts already does with `await` inside try.

Fix `plugins/catalog/src/components/CatalogEntityPage/EntityRenamedNotice.tsx` for these problems, changing only what they need, following the conventions in the shared brief:
1. minor (line 26): `dismissed` is plain local state that is never reset. CatalogEntityPage stays mounted across entity-to-entity navigation, so after the user dismisses one notice, a later rename redirect within the same page instance never shows its notice. The TechDocs counterpart avoids this with `key={formerEntityRef}`. — fix: Store the dismissed ref (`useState<string>()`) and hide the notice only when `dismissedRef === formerEntityRef`, or reset `dismissed` when formerEntityRef changes.

1. minor (line 5): 'Names that no entity has ever used still show the not-found page' is inaccurate. The not-found page also appears for a former name declared by several entities, for one declared by an entity the user cannot read, and for any old name that is not listed in `backstage.io/former-names`. The plan's wording was 'unknown names keep showing the not-found page'. — fix: Reword to: 'Names that cannot be resolved to a single current entity still show the not-found page.'
